speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty; could you tell me exactly when these symptoms started in relation to your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the pain is shooting and triggered by eating or touching the ear, could you tell me exactly where the pain radiates and if you have noticed any changes in your ear canal, such as swelling, drainage, or a feeling of fullness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain triggered by eating and touching the ear suggests involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve. Can you describe if the pain shoots towards your temple or jaw, and do you have any numbness or tingling in your cheek or lower lip? REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Otoscopy shows intact tympanic membranes bilaterally with no signs of active infection, perforation, or cholesteatoma. The right ear shows signs consistent with recent tympanoplasty healing. Clinical findings correlate with auriculotemporal nerve involvement: right postauricular tapping causes tenderness in the right tonsillar area, mandibular palpation reveals no tenderness or jaw clicking, and the preauricular area is non-tender. No numbness or tingling was reported in the cheek or lower lip.
